title: Orbital-Angular-Momentum Entangled Photon Emission From Circular Currents In Semiconductor-Superconductor Structures
authors: Avi Koriat, Ankit Kumar, Alex Hayat
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically demonstrate that a superconducting circular current induced in a semiconductor results in emission of orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) entangled photon pairs upon carrier recombination. Combining the macroscopic Ginzburg-Landau theory and the microscopic Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) theory, we investigate the emission of a superconducting light-emitting diode (SLED) with a spatially varying phase profile in the superconducting order parameter. We show that in the active region of the SLED with a circular supercurrent, radiative recombination processes inherit the order parameter phase and result in photon pairs emitted into modes of different OAM quantum numbers. We demonstrate that coherent superposition of superconducting qubit eigenstates can also be mapped onto a coherent superposition of emitted photon states. We also show that other recombination processes due to thermally excited quasi particles do not significantly degrade the state purity. Our results introduce an original scheme for generating OAM-entangled photons enabling a new method of transmitting superconducting qubit information to photonic channels thereby bridging the gap between solid-state and photon-based platforms for quantum communications and information processing.
tldr: The paper proposes a scheme to generate orbital-angular-momentum entangled photon pairs from circular supercurrents in a semiconductor-superconductor structure, enabling a bridge between superconducting qubits and photonic quantum communication.
motivation: To develop a method for converting superconducting qubit information into photonic channels, which is crucial for quantum networks and communication.
method: Combines Ginzburg-Landau and BCS theories to model a superconducting light-emitting diode (SLED) with a circular supercurrent, where radiative recombination inherits the order parameter phase, producing OAM-entangled photon pairs.
result: Photon pairs are emitted into modes with different OAM quantum numbers, and coherent superpositions of superconducting qubit states are mapped onto photon states; thermal quasiparticles do not significantly degrade purity.
conclusion: This work introduces a new platform for generating OAM-entangled photons, potentially enabling quantum communication between solid-state and photonic systems.

title: Gravitational Entanglement In Optomechanics: Distinguishing Classical And Quantum Models
authors: Samuel Schlegel, Ankit Kumar, Tomasz Paterek, Borivoje Daki\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Observation of gravitationally induced quantum entanglement is often interpreted as a direct evidence of non-classical gravity. While the form and the degree of non-classicality have been rigorously studied from a foundational perspective, classical models reproducing experimental signatures of such entanglement remain underexplored. Motivated by the experimental simplicity, nearly all existing optomechanical approaches assume Gaussian initial states, and due to the weakness of gravity the quantum Newtonian potential is truncated at the second order. However, this regime admits a classical description in terms of the Wigner-Weyl representation, including features typically associated with quantum entanglement. A clear distinction between classical and quantum predictions emerges only beyond this setting. We comprehensively analyze the possibilities and provide operational witnesses for detection of non-classicality via Wigner negativity, and detection of non-quantumness via negativity of the Weyl operator. Our results demonstrate that the experimental requirements on certifying gravitational entanglement are more stringent than previously anticipated.
tldr: This paper shows that Gaussian optomechanical models of gravitational entanglement can be mimicked by classical Wigner-Weyl descriptions, requiring non-Gaussian features to certify non-classical gravity.
motivation: To clarify whether observed gravitational entanglement necessarily implies non-classical gravity, as classical models may reproduce Gaussian entanglement signatures.
method: The authors analyze optomechanical setups with Gaussian initial states and quadratic Newtonian potential, using Wigner-Weyl representation to compare classical and quantum predictions, and propose operational witnesses based on Wigner negativity and Weyl operator negativity.
result: Gaussian optomechanical entanglement can be explained classically; true quantumness requires non-Gaussian states or higher-order interactions, making experimental certification more demanding.
conclusion: Future experiments must go beyond Gaussian assumptions to unambiguously demonstrate gravitational entanglement as evidence of non-classical gravity.

title: Resource Generation And Dynamical Complexities In Open Random Quantum Circuits
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Arkaprava Sil, Priya Ghosh, Ujjwal Sen, Sudipto Singha Roy
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Realistic quantum devices are inherently open and often involve environments with memory. Here, we investigate quantum resource generation in two classes of random circuits, namely, memoryless open and memoryful open random circuits, and compare their behavior with the well-explored random unitary circuit model. We show that environmental memory qualitatively alters the dynamics: while unitary and memoryful circuits exhibit sustained growth and saturation of entanglement and non-stabilizerness (magic); memoryless dynamics leads to a distinct behavior where entanglement decays to zero after transient growth, even though non-stabilizerness remains non-zero, indicating the persistence of nonclassical features beyond entanglement. Consistently, Krylov complexity reveals suppressed spreading of quantum states in memoryless circuits, in contrast to strong growth in unitary and memoryful dynamics, which saturates at the maximum value. Finally, we show that memoryful circuits more effectively approach low-order quantum-state k-designs than the other two circuits. Closed dynamics are therefore usually the most resource-generating, but are ideal; realistic dynamics are open and seem to generate less, but if they possess memory, they can sometimes even outdo closed dynamics.
tldr: This paper studies how environmental memory affects entanglement and non-stabilizerness generation in open random quantum circuits, showing that memoryful circuits can sometimes outperform closed dynamics.
motivation: Realistic quantum devices are open and often have memory, but most studies focus on memoryless or unitary circuits. Understanding resource generation in memoryful open circuits is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors compare three classes of random circuits: unitary (closed), memoryless open, and memoryful open (with environmental memory). They compute entanglement entropy, non-stabilizerness (magic), Krylov complexity, and approach to k-designs.
result: Memoryless circuits show entanglement decay after transient growth, while non-stabilizerness remains nonzero. Memoryful circuits sustain entanglement growth similar to unitary circuits and can even exceed them in approaching k-designs.
conclusion: Environmental memory qualitatively changes resource generation dynamics, and memoryful open circuits can be more resourceful than closed ones, suggesting that realistic open systems with memory may be advantageous for quantum information tasks.

title: Compact Narrowband Photon-pair Generation By Slow-light Spectral Engineering
authors: Elizabeth A. Goldschmidt Ashwith Prabhu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficiently generating photon pairs with high heralding efficiency and high single photon purity that are bandwidth matched to quantum emitters, quantum memories, and other matter-based qubits is critical for quantum networking applications. However, nonlinear optics-based sources require substantial spectral engineering to overcome the orders of magnitude bandwidth mismatch between those sources and qubit systems. A popular solution is cavity-enhanced spontaneous parametric down conversion (SPDC) where the cavity sets the photon bandwidth and simultaneously enhances the spectral brightness of the SPDC. Bulk, free-space configurations are generally required to achieve the MHz-scale bandwidths required to interface with most qubit systems. Replicating these in scalable integrated photonic architectures is an ongoing challenge due to the much higher propagation losses that limit the size and linewidth of chip-based resonators. We show here how an intra-cavity slow light medium, acting as an ultra-narrow filter, would enable narrowband photon pair generation in broadband cavities with high single photon purity and without compromising the heralding efficiency. We show that such metrics can be readily realized in erbium doped thin-film lithium niobate microrings using realistic design parameters.
tldr: This paper proposes using an intra-cavity slow-light medium to generate narrowband photon pairs in broadband integrated resonators, enabling MHz-scale bandwidths for quantum networking.
motivation: Efficient photon-pair sources with narrow bandwidths matched to quantum memories and emitters are critical for quantum networks, but integrated photonic resonators suffer from high losses limiting their linewidth. This work aims to overcome that limitation.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a cavity-enhanced SPDC source incorporating a slow-light medium (e.g., erbium-doped lithium niobate) as an ultra-narrow filter inside a broadband microring resonator, using realistic design parameters.
result: They show that such a configuration can achieve narrowband photon-pair generation with high single-photon purity and high heralding efficiency, without requiring high-finesse cavities.
conclusion: This approach offers a path to scalable, integrated narrowband photon-pair sources for quantum repeaters and memory interfaces, with potential for on-chip integration.

title: Strongly-coupled non-Markovian Waveguide Qed With Input-output Heom
authors: Neill Lambert, Yi-Te Huang, Yueh-Nan Chen, Paul Menczel, Franco Nori
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of modeling a single qubit in contact with a one-dimensional waveguide beyond the standard perturbative and Markovian approximations. Using the recently developed input-output hierarchical equations of motion (io-HEOM), we investigate multiple examples of such waveguides, characterized by different spectral densities. Our examples highlight that the io-HEOM method can accurately capture non-Markovianity in waveguide QED from two distinct origins. The first source of non-Markovianity is spatially non-local coupling between the qubit and the waveguide. By examining two examples with non-local coupling, we show how the coupling function affects the steady-state bound photons, and demonstrate the release of these photons when the qubit energy is quenched. The second source of non-Markovianity is non-linear dispersion. We illustrate this scenario using the example of a cavity array with point-like coupling, where the non-linear dispersion leads to persistent oscillations due to Van Hove singularities in the spectral density.
tldr: This paper applies the input-output hierarchical equations of motion (io-HEOM) to model non-Markovian waveguide QED beyond perturbative approximations.
motivation: Standard waveguide QED relies on Markovian and perturbative approximations, which fail in strongly coupled regimes. The authors aim to accurately capture non-Markovian effects from spatially non-local coupling and nonlinear dispersion.
method: The io-HEOM method is used to simulate a qubit coupled to a 1D waveguide with various spectral densities, including non-local coupling and cavity array dispersion.
result: The method captures two distinct sources of non-Markovianity: spatially non-local coupling leads to bound photons that can be released via qubit energy quenching, and nonlinear dispersion causes persistent oscillations due to Van Hove singularities.
conclusion: The io-HEOM is a powerful tool for strongly coupled waveguide QED, enabling accurate modeling of non-Markovian effects relevant for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.

authors: Farhad Farokhi

For any [MATH]-qubit probe state, where [MATH] denotes the number of sensors, [MATH] for all unit orthogonal sensing directions [MATH] and [MATH], with equality for all equatorial states when [MATH] and for Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states when [MATH]. Heisenberg-limited precision for direction [MATH], [MATH], saturates the bound and simultaneously forces zero QFI for all other independent directions. This can be interpreted as the condition for parameter privacy in distributed quantum sensing: attaining Heisenberg-limited precision for the sensing target renders all alternative privacy-intrusive estimations impossible.
tldr: Establishes a quantum Fisher information duality for distributed quantum sensor networks, showing that Heisenberg-limited precision for one sensing direction forces zero QFI for all orthogonal directions, enabling parameter privacy.
motivation: To understand the fundamental trade-off between precision and privacy in distributed quantum sensing networks, and to derive conditions under which Heisenberg-limited precision can be achieved while preventing privacy-intrusive estimations.
method: Theoretical analysis using quantum Fisher information (QFI) for distributed sensor networks with local phase encoding. Derives a duality relation for QFI along orthogonal sensing directions and examines its saturation for equatorial and GHZ states.
result: For any N-qubit probe state, QFI along orthogonal directions sum to N^2, with equality for equatorial states (N=2) and GHZ states (N≥2). Heisenberg-limited precision for one direction forces zero QFI for all other independent directions, interpreted as parameter privacy.
conclusion: The QFI duality provides a fundamental bound linking precision and privacy in distributed quantum sensing, with implications for secure quantum sensing and network design. Future work may explore experimental realizations and extensions to other probe states.

title: Multi-Qubit Entanglement Of Unit Cell Pairs In SiMOS
authors: Cameron Jones, Jonathan Y. Huang, Santiago Serrano, Mengke Feng, Gerardo A. Paz-Silva, Tuomo Tanttu, Paul Steinacker, Fay E. Hudson, Wee Han Lim, Nikolay V. Abrosimov, Hans-Joachim Pohl, Michael L. W. Thewalt, Andrew S. Dzurak, Andre Saraiva, Arne Laucht, Chih Hwan Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin qubits in silicon-MOS (SiMOS) quantum dots have recently demonstrated compatibility with existing industry standard CMOS fabrication techniques. These devices have routinely achieved single- and two-qubit gate fidelities above 99% and demonstrated highly entangled two-qubit Bell states in isolated double quantum dot (DQD) unit cells, however coupling between unit cells has remained challenging. In this work, we present a two unit cell, four-qubit SiMOS processor with universal controllability and fully parallelised state initialisation and readout. We use this processor to generate maximally entangled three-qubit states, including the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state, and certify multipartite entanglement through violation of the classical Mermin-witness bound. By using a fully symmetric dynamically decoupled gate sequence to create our entangled states, we are able to preserve the lifetime of the entanglement beyond [MATH], to a time limited instead by [MATH]. These demonstrations pave a road to the scalable operation of larger SiMOS processors, and achieving high purity, long-lived multi-qubit entangled states in them.
tldr: Demonstration of multi-qubit entanglement (GHZ states) in a four-qubit SiMOS quantum dot processor with high fidelity and long coherence times.
motivation: To scale silicon-based quantum processors beyond single unit cells by demonstrating inter-cell coupling and multi-qubit entanglement.
method: Fabrication of a two-unit-cell, four-qubit SiMOS processor with full control and parallel readout; use of dynamically decoupled gate sequences to generate and preserve entangled states.
result: Generation and certification of three-qubit GHZ states violating the Mermin witness bound, with entanglement lifetime limited by T2* rather than T1.
conclusion: Paves the way for scalable SiMOS quantum processors with long-lived multi-qubit entanglement, relevant for quantum communication and computation.

title: Decoy Statebased Time Synchronization
authors: Lukas Tiefenthaler, Hannah Thiel, Davide Rusca, Antia Lamaslinares
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time synchronization is a crucial requirement in quantum key distribution (QKD)8 protocols, ensuring accurate key generation via the correct assignment of bits of raw key and9 enabling eavesdropping detection via the precise recording of photon statistics. State-of-the-art10 experiments typically use an extra channel to synchronize the clocks of the transmitter and receiver11 via classical signals. In this work, we study the possibility of performing clock synchronization12 via the signals used for the key generation, which are already present in decoy-state-based BB8413 protocols.14 Without altering the protocol in any way, we use the different mean photon numbers of the15 signal and decoy states for time synchronization without a dedicated physical channel capable of16 clock synchronization. The proposed method relies only on the photons sent and received for17 key generation and does not require any change to the QKD protocol. The only change in the18 experiment is on the software level, thus making it very simple to implement.19 We demonstrate clock synchronization method in a simulation of a specific fiber-based QKD20 experiment. Like other decoy-state-based BB84 protocols, it is based on weak coherent pulses.21 In this simulation, we investigate the parameter space to find limits and optimal choices of our22 proposed method.23 In addition to the non-protocol-altering clock synchronization method, we also discuss an24 approach that significantly improves performance in lossy channels by introducing an additional25 decoy state with a very high mean photon number.26 By eliminating the need for an extra channel capable of clock synchronization, both methods27 proposed potentially reduce the complexity and cost of QKD systems and improve their agility.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to perform clock synchronization in decoy-state BB84 QKD using the existing quantum signals, eliminating the need for a dedicated classical synchronization channel.
motivation: Time synchronization is critical for QKD but typically requires an extra classical channel, increasing complexity and cost. The authors aim to leverage the decoy-state protocol's inherent signal variations for synchronization without altering the protocol.
method: The method uses the different mean photon numbers of signal and decoy states to extract timing information from the received photon statistics, implemented via software-level changes only. A simulation of a fiber-based QKD experiment is used to explore parameter space and optimize performance.
result: The proposed method achieves clock synchronization without an extra channel, and an additional high-mean-photon-number decoy state improves performance in lossy channels. The simulation identifies optimal parameters and limits.
conclusion: This work reduces QKD system complexity and cost by eliminating a dedicated synchronization channel, potentially improving agility. Future work could extend to other QKD protocols or experimental validation.

title: Entangling Power: A Probe Of Symmetry And Integrability In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Pallab Goswami Ian Low
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The entangling power of a unitary operator quantifies its ability to generate entanglement from product states and provides a natural probe of quantum many-body dynamics. Entanglement extremization at points of enhanced symmetry has previously been observed in high-energy scattering. In this work we compute the time-averaged entangling power of anisotropic Heisenberg spin chains across two-site models and finite-size systems, as well as the entangling power of the two-magnon [MATH]-matrix in the thermodynamic limit. For two-site models we establish a monotonic hierarchy: the entangling power decreases as the symmetry group grows, reaching its minimum at the [MATH] XXX point. Finite-size XXZ chains exhibit sharp dips at the [MATH] points [MATH] and the free-fermion point [MATH], with the free-fermion dip decaying much more slowly with system size. In the thermodynamic limit, we decompose the two-magnon [MATH]-matrix into quantum logic gates -- Identity, SWAP, and [MATH] -- and show that the entangling power vanishes for all scattering energies at the [MATH] points, where the [MATH]-matrix reduces to the Identity gate, while the free-fermion point achieves the maximum -- the opposite of the finite-size many-body behavior. The entangling power can serve as an {\em operator} diagnostic for symmetry and selected aspects of integrability in quantum simulations of spin-chain dynamics.
tldr: The paper studies the entangling power of unitary operators in spin chains as a probe of symmetry and integrability, finding that entangling power extremizes at points of enhanced symmetry.
motivation: To understand how entanglement generation relates to symmetries and integrability in quantum many-body systems, and to provide an operator-level diagnostic for quantum simulations.
method: Analytical and numerical computation of time-averaged entangling power for two-site models and finite-size XXZ chains, and decomposition of the two-magnon S-matrix into quantum gates in the thermodynamic limit.
result: Entangling power decreases with larger symmetry groups in two-site models; finite-size chains show sharp dips at SU(2) and free-fermion points; in the thermodynamic limit, entangling power vanishes at SU(2) points and is maximal at the free-fermion point.
conclusion: Entangling power serves as a useful operator diagnostic for symmetry and integrability, with potential applications in quantum simulations of spin-chain dynamics.

title: Hamiltonian And Symplectic Tensors In The T-product Algebra
authors: Taehyeong Kim Susana Lopez-Moreno
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Hamiltonian and symplectic tensor structures in the T-product algebra. We define T-Hamiltonian and T-symplectic tensors and characterize them through their Fourier-domain slices. For T-Hamiltonian tensors we establish the standard block form and the spectral symmetry of T-eigenvalues, while for T-symplectic tensors we derive the inverse and exponential-map properties. Our main result is a constructive T-Williamson normal form for tensors whose Fourier-domain slices are real symmetric positive-definite matrices. We also show that, under the Hermitian symplectic convention adopted here, this decomposition does not extend directly to arbitrary Hermitian positive-definite Fourier-domain slices, and we derive a real-valued recovery criterion under Fourier conjugate symmetry. Numerical experiments verify the construction, exhibit runtime trends consistent with the slice-wise complexity [MATH], and illustrate the framework on a Fourier-domain encoding of covariance-matrix families arising in continuous-variable quantum dynamics.
tldr: This paper develops a T-product algebra framework for Hamiltonian and symplectic tensors, with applications to continuous-variable quantum dynamics.
motivation: To extend symplectic and Hamiltonian structures to the T-product algebra, enabling efficient analysis of tensor-valued systems arising in quantum optics and continuous-variable quantum information.
method: The authors define T-Hamiltonian and T-symplectic tensors, characterize them via Fourier-domain slices, and derive a constructive T-Williamson normal form for tensors with real symmetric positive-definite Fourier slices.
result: They establish spectral symmetry for T-Hamiltonian tensors, inverse and exponential-map properties for T-symplectic tensors, and a real-valued recovery criterion under Fourier conjugate symmetry. Numerical experiments verify the construction.
conclusion: The T-Williamson normal form provides a powerful tool for analyzing covariance matrices in continuous-variable quantum systems, though extension to arbitrary Hermitian positive-definite slices is not straightforward.

title: Room-temperature THz Photon Detection Via Nonlinear Upconversion With 2% Full-system Efficiency
authors: Aswin Vishnuradhan (department Of Physics, University Of Ottawa, Ottawa, Ontario K1N 6N5, Canada), Wei Cui (department Of Physics, University Of Ottawa, Ottawa, Ontario K1N 6N5, Canada), Hesam Heydarian (department Of Physics, University Of Ottawa, Ottawa, Ontario K1N 6N5, Canada), Eeswar Kumar Yalavarthi (department Of Physics, University Of Ottawa, Ottawa, Ontario K1N 6N5, Canada), Nicolas Couture (department Of Physics, University Of Ottawa, Ottawa, Ontario K1N 6N5, Canada), Alain Villeneuve (consultants Optav Inc, Mont-Royal, Qu\'ebec, Canada), Angela Gamouras (department Of Physics, University Of Ottawa, Ottawa, Ontario K1N 6N5, Canada, National Research Council Canada, Montreal Road, Ottawa, Ontario, Canada), Jean-Michel M\'enard
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sensitive detection of terahertz (THz) radiation is fundamental to progress in spectroscopy, advanced wireless communication, and the realization of emerging quantum technologies. However, the intrinsically low photon energies in the THz range combined with thermal background radiation tend to constrain detector performance when operating at ambient temperatures. Here, we demonstrate efficient room-temperature THz detection based on nonlinear upconversion in the organic crystal N-benzyl-2-methyl-4-nitroaniline (BNA) to resolve frequencies from 1 to 7.5 THz. The system encompassing spectral filters and a single-photon counter achieves an overall detection efficiency of 2% for sum-frequency generated photons. This enables the detection of a train of 50 000 terahertz pulses carrying, on average, fewer than 0.04 photons per pulse, with a signal-to-noise ratio of unity. At a higher flux, when ~60 photons per pulse impinge on the BNA crystal, the per-pulse detection probability reaches 50%. After accounting for loss mechanisms in the setup, the nonlinear THz-to-near-infrared conversion efficiency in BNA exceeds 75%. These results demonstrate the feasibility of quantum experiments relying on single-photon-level THz detection via upconversion in nonlinear crystals in ambient conditions.
tldr: This paper demonstrates room-temperature THz photon detection via nonlinear upconversion in an organic crystal, achieving 2% full-system efficiency and single-photon-level sensitivity.
motivation: Sensitive THz detection is crucial for spectroscopy, wireless communication, and quantum technologies, but low photon energies and thermal background limit performance at room temperature.
method: The authors use nonlinear upconversion in the organic crystal BNA to convert THz photons to near-infrared, which are then detected by a single-photon counter, with spectral filters to reduce noise.
result: The system achieves 2% overall detection efficiency, can detect pulses with <0.04 photons per pulse at SNR=1, and 50% detection probability at ~60 photons per pulse; internal conversion efficiency exceeds 75%.
conclusion: This work enables quantum experiments with single-photon-level THz detection at room temperature, potentially advancing quantum communication and sensing in the THz regime.

title: Mean-field And Fluctuation Dynamics In Off-resonant Two-mode Atom-field Interactions
authors: Luis Medina-Dozal, Alejandro R. Urz\'ua, Carlos A. Gonz\'alez-Guti\'errez, Jos\'e R\'ecamier
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a two-level system coupled to two quantized electromagnetic modes within the Jaynes-Cummings framework. While the single-mode model is exactly solvable due to its conserved excitation number, yielding finite-dimensional invariant subspaces, the two-mode model extension presents a fundamental challenge: although the total excitation number remains conserved, each invariant subspace is infinite-dimensional, preventing a closed-form analytical solution. Our scheme separates the dynamics into a dominant, exactly solvable semiclassical component, the atom interacting with the mean fields of both modes, and treats the remaining quantum fluctuations through a sequence of unitary transformations that preserve essential quantum features. We validate our approach through direct comparison with numerical solutions, focusing on the non-resonant regime where multiple detunings give rise to rich interference effects and multi-timescale dynamics inaccessible to standard approximations. The method accurately reproduces atomic inversion, field observables, and fidelity over relevant timescales, while remaining computationally efficient.
tldr: This paper develops a mean-field plus fluctuation method to solve the two-mode Jaynes-Cummings model in the off-resonant regime, capturing multi-timescale dynamics efficiently.
motivation: The two-mode Jaynes-Cummings model is not exactly solvable due to infinite-dimensional invariant subspaces, and standard approximations fail in the off-resonant regime with multiple detunings.
method: The dynamics are separated into a dominant semiclassical mean-field component and quantum fluctuations treated via a sequence of unitary transformations, preserving quantum features.
result: The method accurately reproduces atomic inversion, field observables, and fidelity compared to numerical solutions, while being computationally efficient.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for studying multi-mode quantum optics systems, with potential applications in quantum information and hybrid quantum systems.

title: WSi Weak Link Element With A Non-sinusoidal Current-phase Relation
authors: Sarah Garcia Jones, Trevyn F. Q. Larson, Sai Pavan Chitta, Heli Vora, Varun Verma, Sae Woo Nam, Jos\'e Aumentado, Jens Koch, Raymond W. Simmonds, Andr\'as Gyenis
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinearity is an essential ingredient for encoding quantum states with non-uniform energy spacing, implementing coherent quantum gates, reading out qubits, amplifying, and mixing electromagnetic signals. In this work, we demonstrate the nonlinear behavior of a constriction fabricated from an amorphous, high-kinetic inductance material, tungsten silicide, embedded in a three-dimensional RF-SQUID. We find that the results are consistent with the weak link behaving as a Josephson junction with a sawtooth-like current-phase relation or a quantum phase slip element. Finally, we measure relaxation times of the metastable, persistent-current states trapped in the local minima of the potential.
tldr: This paper demonstrates nonlinear behavior in a tungsten silicide weak link embedded in an RF-SQUID, consistent with a sawtooth current-phase relation or quantum phase slip element.
motivation: Nonlinearity is crucial for quantum state encoding, gates, readout, and signal processing; the work explores high-kinetic inductance materials for such applications.
method: Fabrication of a constriction from amorphous tungsten silicide in a 3D RF-SQUID, followed by measurements of current-phase relation and relaxation times of persistent-current states.
result: The weak link exhibits a sawtooth-like current-phase relation, characteristic of a Josephson junction or quantum phase slip element; relaxation times of metastable states were measured.
conclusion: The findings highlight the potential of high-kinetic inductance materials for nonlinear quantum devices, with implications for hybrid quantum systems and superconducting circuits.

title: Bowtie VarQTE: A Resource-Efficient Quantum State Preparation Primitive
authors: Marc Drudis, Alberto Baiardi, Mattia Chiurco, Francesco Tacchino, Stefan Woerner, Christa Zoufal
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The preparation of quantum states is a fundamental requirement for many quantum algorithms. A native route to preparing physically structured states is based on short-time simulation of dynamical processes, such as real or imaginary time evolution. This work presents a resource-efficient framework for the approximation thereof with } which uses classical simulation where possible and quantum resources where necessary. We introduce a framework that leverages existing causal light-cones to minimize quantum resource requirements in the evaluation of gradient and quantum geometric tensor terms by utilizing classical simulation methods for causally relevant subcircuits. This in turn enables exact parameter updates according to McLachlan's variational principle and, thereby, improves numerical stability. We conduct a comparison with a state preparation method that is based on a tensor-network compiled Trotter algorithm: approximate quantum compilation (AQC). In recent work, this approach has shown impressive performance. However, its key-bottleneck is the necessity to have a classical (approximate) representation of the target state. Our numerical experiments indicate that bowtie VarQTE can achieve comparable fidelities without this requirement. We further illustrate how bowtie VarQTE can facilitate a state-preparation pipeline that combines the simulation of imaginary and real time evolution for a sample-based quantum algorithm. In fact, results on 2D systems show how bowtie VarQTE can reduce the quantum requirements compared to standard, sample-based Krylov diagonalization calculations. Our results indicate that VarQTE is a promising primitive for the preparation of physically structured quantum states that reduces requirements on quantum resources by leveraging existing structures and the associated possibility of enabling classical simulations.
tldr: Bowtie VarQTE is a resource-efficient quantum state preparation method that uses classical simulation of causal light-cones to reduce quantum resource requirements.
motivation: To prepare physically structured quantum states efficiently for quantum algorithms, overcoming the need for a classical representation of the target state.
method: The framework leverages causal light-cones to classically simulate subcircuits, enabling exact parameter updates via McLachlan's variational principle.
result: Bowtie VarQTE achieves fidelities comparable to tensor-network compiled Trotter methods without requiring a classical target state representation, and reduces quantum resources in 2D systems.
conclusion: The method is a promising primitive for state preparation, reducing quantum resource demands by exploiting structure and classical simulation.

title: Interpreting Bohm Quantum Potentials In Computing Quantum Waves Exactly From Classical Action
authors: Jean-Jacques Slotine Winfried Lohmiller
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recent arXiv posting [11], commenting on the paper [7], argues that the proof of Lemma 3.1 in [7] is missing the Bohm quantum potential [1, 2] of the Madelung p.d.e. [9]. This short technical note extends the proof of Lemma 3.1 to introduce a Bohm quantum potential explicitly, and then shows why this term can be assumed to be zero in the wave construction, without loss of generality. The continuity p.d.e. and the Hamilton-Jacobi p.d.e., extended by the Bohm potential, are undisputed. However, the actual action and density solutions depend on their initialization at t = 0. In [7], this initialization is motivated by the Feynman kernel [4], which is fundamentally different from the standard initialization of the Madelung solution [9]. This in turn leads to different action and density solutions, and explains why in one case the Bohm quantum potential disappears and in the other does not. The resulting overall wave, however, is independent of this computational initialization.
tldr: This note extends a lemma to include the Bohm quantum potential and argues it can be set to zero under a specific initialization based on the Feynman kernel, without affecting the overall wavefunction.
motivation: To address a criticism that a previous proof omitted the Bohm quantum potential, and to clarify why the potential vanishes under the chosen initialization.
method: The authors extend Lemma 3.1 by explicitly introducing the Bohm potential into the Madelung equations, then show that with the Feynman kernel initialization the potential term becomes zero.
result: The Bohm quantum potential can be assumed zero in the wave construction without loss of generality when using the Feynman kernel initialization, leading to different action and density solutions but the same overall wave.
conclusion: The wavefunction is independent of the computational initialization, reconciling the two approaches.

title: Quantum End-to-End Learning For Contextual Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Changhyun Kwon Jaehwan Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contextual combinatorial optimization (CCO) plays a critical role in decision-making under uncertainty, yet remains a significant challenge. We present Quantum End-to-End Learning (QEL), the first quantum computing-based end-to-end learning framework for CCO that leverages Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms. Inspired by the integration of state preparation and evolution in data re-uploading, we propose a context re-uploading phase-separator that jointly captures the complex relations among contexts, uncertain coefficients, and optimal solutions. This allows a contextual encoder to be seamlessly integrated within a quantum surrogate policy, enabling joint end-to-end training with a stationarity guarantee. Exploiting an optimization-aware structure grounded in physical principles that classical methods cannot readily leverage, our approach demonstrates practicality by directly training on task loss despite the discreteness and nonconvexity, while avoiding calls to NP-hard optimization solvers. QEL empirically achieves competitive performance while requiring substantially fewer parameters than classical benchmarks, highlighting its industrial-level potential for the future quantum era.

motivation: Contextual combinatorial optimization is important for decision-making under uncertainty, and classical methods face challenges in handling complex contexts and nonconvex losses.
method: The authors introduce Quantum End-to-End Learning (QEL), which integrates a context re-uploading phase-separator within a QAOA-based quantum surrogate policy, enabling joint end-to-end training with a stationarity guarantee.
result: QEL achieves competitive performance with substantially fewer parameters than classical benchmarks, demonstrating practicality without requiring NP-hard solvers.
conclusion: The approach shows potential for industrial-level applications in the quantum era, but its relevance to the user's specific research areas is limited.

title: Mechanism Of Efficacy In Qaoa For Random k-SAT: From Adiabatic Manifold To Sublinear Parameter Optimization
authors: Hanwu Chen Mingyou Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is a leading candidate for demonstrating quantum advantage on near-term devices, yet the physical origins of its efficacy remain poorly understood. In this work, we study QAOA for random [MATH]-SAT problems within a universal-mixer [MATH]-local search framework, establishing a formal correspondence between adiabatic state transfer and the QAOA ansatz. This correspondence yields a rigorous performance guarantee for random instances with clause density [MATH] and circuit depth [MATH]. We further investigate the NISQ regime with shallow circuits of depth [MATH]. Surprisingly, the optimal parameters do not become stochastic under depth compression, but instead remain confined to a structured low-dimensional region, which we identify as a smooth adiabatic manifold. Numerical evidence indicates that this manifold persists across different circuit depths and arises from the variational suppression of adiabatic leakage. Based on this structure, we propose the smooth adiabatic-manifold parameterization (SAMP) strategy, transforming parameter optimization from an unstructured high-dimensional search into a guided refinement process. Numerical experiments on random 3-SAT instances show that SAMP achieves sublinear optimization scaling with circuit depth while providing robust zero-cost initialization for deep circuits.
tldr: This paper analyzes the efficacy of QAOA for random k-SAT problems, establishing a correspondence with adiabatic state transfer and proposing a parameter optimization strategy.
motivation: To understand the physical origins of QAOA's efficacy and improve parameter optimization for near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors establish a formal correspondence between adiabatic state transfer and the QAOA ansatz, and propose the smooth adiabatic-manifold parameterization (SAMP) strategy for parameter optimization.
result: Optimal QAOA parameters remain confined to a low-dimensional adiabatic manifold, and SAMP achieves sublinear optimization scaling with circuit depth.
conclusion: The adiabatic manifold structure enables efficient parameter optimization, potentially improving QAOA performance on NISQ devices.

title: Targeting Clause Type Distributions: A Picklock For Random Satisfiability Problems
authors: J. C. Budich J. Schwardt
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimization problems such as the NP-complete 3-SAT provide an important benchmark for the difficult task of finding ground-states in strongly correlated many-body systems with rugged energy landscapes. The study of random 3-SAT problems as Ising spin Hamiltonians in statistical physics has yielded major insights including the existence of a satisfiability phase transition, and the prediction of a critical parameter line of particularly hard instances. Yet, progress on solving those instances has been scarce for several decades. Here, introducing the Target-SAT (TSAT) algorithm, we roughly triple the tractable problem sizes in the hardest regime, with an even greater improvement in a vast range of neighboring regions. By leveraging statistical information hidden in the combinatorial constraints of the problem, TSAT is actively guided in its stochastic local search toward a target within the relevant parameter space. Our analysis also explains why established local search algorithms are limited to relatively small system sizes due to a vast low-energy trap. Furthermore, we characterize the aforementioned critical line in terms of a dominant additional complexity barrier, whose exponential scaling is quickly overcome by TSAT only in the surrounding parameter space. With TSAT, the lead in solving the hardest known random satisfiability problems returns to the realm of stochastic local search algorithms.
tldr: The paper introduces the Target-SAT algorithm that improves solving of random 3-SAT problems by leveraging statistical information in clause type distributions.
motivation: To overcome the difficulty of solving hard random 3-SAT instances, which serve as benchmarks for optimization problems in many-body systems.
method: The TSAT algorithm uses stochastic local search guided by statistical information from combinatorial constraints to target specific parameter space regions.
result: TSAT roughly triples the tractable problem sizes in the hardest regime and shows even greater improvement in neighboring regions, overcoming a low-energy trap that limits other algorithms.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that stochastic local search can still lead progress in solving hard random satisfiability problems, with implications for understanding complexity barriers.

title: Halving The Cost Of Qrom
authors: Matthew Pocrnic Danial Motlagh

It involves the coherent loading of [MATH] bitstrings of length [MATH] in superposition, and naively has a non-Clifford cost of [MATH] Toffolis. It is known that given access to [MATH] dirty qubits, one can reduce the Toffoli cost of QROM to [MATH]. In this work, we first present an optimization to reduce this cost to [MATH] by replacing the ``SelectSwap" architecture with ``SelectCopy". We then provide a further optimization for the qubit-constrained regime where the Toffoli cost is typically [MATH], and reduce it to [MATH], cutting the cost by approximately [MATH] and effectively matching the performance of clean-qubit QROM using dirty qubits for practical values of [MATH]. Lastly, we provide a parametric family of methods that allow the interpolation of the prefactor of the [MATH] term from [MATH] to ([MATH]) to obtain the best cost for different qubit availability regimes.

method: The authors replace the SelectSwap architecture with SelectCopy to reduce Toffoli cost from O(λ) to O(λ/2) when dirty qubits are available, and further optimize for qubit-constrained regimes to match clean-qubit performance.
