title: Higher-Rank Connections And Deformed Schr\"odinger Operators
authors: Jonah Baerman, Alba Grassi, Giovanni Ravazzini
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the connection problem for a class of linear differential equations of order [MATH] closely related to the Baxter equation of the quantum Toda chain. The space of solutions is [MATH]-dimensional and several linearly independent solutions decay at each singularity, leading to a rich structure of boundary value problems. We derive the weakest quantization conditions compatible with decaying behavior at both singularities, and formulate these conditions in terms of the associated monodromy data. In doing so, we prove the quantization conditions predicted by the topological string/spectral theory duality for a family of deformed Schr\"odinger equations. More generally, our results point to a hierarchy of spectral problems interpolating between the minimal conditions studied here and the maximally decaying boundary conditions of the [MATH]-particle quantum Toda chain.
tldr: This paper studies connection problems for higher-order linear differential equations related to the quantum Toda chain, deriving quantization conditions via monodromy data and confirming topological string/spectral theory duality.
motivation: To understand the boundary value problems and quantization conditions for a class of differential equations arising from the quantum Toda chain, and to prove predictions from topological string/spectral theory duality.
method: Analytical study of linear differential equations of order N, analysis of monodromy data, and derivation of quantization conditions for decaying solutions at singularities.
result: Derived the weakest quantization conditions compatible with decaying behavior at both singularities, formulated in terms of monodromy data, and proved the quantization conditions predicted by the topological string/spectral theory duality for deformed Schrödinger equations.
conclusion: The results point to a hierarchy of spectral problems interpolating between minimal and maximally decaying boundary conditions, with implications for the quantum Toda chain and spectral theory.

title: Forced Gap Post-Selection For Quantum Ldpc Codes And Their Operations
authors: Adam Wills, Theodore J. Yoder, Isaac Chuang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a simple and general post-selection strategy for high-rate quantum codes that is transferrable across decoders. After an initial baseline run, the decoder is re-run once per logical observable, and forced in these latter runs to provide a solution where the given observable has the complementary outcome. Shots are rejected that find logically complementary solutions with similar likelihoods compared to the baseline. Using the Relay-BP decoder, we benchmark the strategy on the [MATH]-qubit and [MATH]-qubit bivariate bicycle codes, as well as surgery gadgets for the latter. In comparison to previous post-selection strategies, our results offer an improved logical error rate by over a factor of [MATH] on the same circuit and physical error rate, and at the same rate of post-selection. Our strategies are also lightweight, relying only on FPGA-friendly belief propagation, whereas the previous best used repeated rounds of a high-latency BP-OSD decoder.
tldr: This paper introduces a forced gap post-selection strategy for quantum LDPC codes to improve logical error rates using lightweight belief propagation decoding.
motivation: To reduce logical error rates in high-rate quantum codes without relying on high-latency decoders, enabling practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The decoder is run once per logical observable with forced complementary outcomes; shots with similar likelihoods for both outcomes are rejected. The strategy is benchmarked on bivariate bicycle codes using the Relay-BP decoder.
result: The forced gap post-selection improves logical error rate by over a factor of 2 compared to previous post-selection strategies at the same post-selection rate, using only FPGA-friendly belief propagation.
conclusion: This lightweight post-selection method is transferable across decoders and offers practical improvements for quantum LDPC codes, with potential for hardware implementation.

title: Sampling Noise And Optimized Measurement Distribution In Imaginary-Time Quantum Dynamics Simulations
authors: Feng Zhang, Niladri Gomes, Joshua Aftergood, Thomas Iadecola, Yong-Xin Yao, Peter P. Orth
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variational quantum dynamics simulations (VQDS) provide a promising route to simulate real- and imaginary-time quantum dynamics on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices using fixed-depth circuits. However, their practical performance is strongly limited by sampling noise arising from a finite number of circuit measurements. In this work, we systematically investigate the impact of sampling noise on VQDS, with a focus on ground-state preparation in one-dimensional Ising spin models using imaginary time evolution. We compare different regularization strategies for stabilizing the equations of motion and show that Tikhonov regularization provides robust performance in noisy imaginary-time evolution. We then benchmark measurement-distribution strategies that allocate shots by minimizing a cost function that characterizes the error in solving the equation of motion. Using noisy circuit simulations, we demonstrate that such optimized shot allocation can significantly improve state fidelity and reduce the total measurement cost by more than a factor of two compared to uniform shot distributions. We observe that the best results are found if a sufficiently large number of measurements is guaranteed for all circuits, suggesting that a finite fraction of shots should be distributed evenly. Our results provide practical guidelines for implementing measurement-efficient variational quantum dynamics and ground-state preparation on near-term quantum hardware.
tldr: This paper studies sampling noise and optimized measurement distribution in variational quantum dynamics simulations for ground-state preparation, focusing on imaginary-time evolution.
motivation: Variational quantum dynamics simulations are promising for near-term quantum devices but are limited by sampling noise from finite measurements. The research aims to understand and mitigate this noise to improve practical performance.
method: The authors systematically investigate sampling noise in imaginary-time VQDS for 1D Ising spin models, comparing regularization strategies (e.g., Tikhonov) and benchmarking measurement-distribution strategies that allocate shots by minimizing a cost function related to equation-of-motion error.
result: Tikhonov regularization provides robust performance under noise. Optimized shot allocation significantly improves state fidelity and reduces total measurement cost by more than a factor of two compared to uniform distributions, with best results when a sufficient number of measurements is guaranteed for all circuits.
conclusion: The results provide practical guidelines for implementing measurement-efficient variational quantum dynamics and ground-state preparation on near-term quantum hardware, emphasizing the importance of balanced shot allocation.

title: Spatio-spectral Vector Light Created By Optical Activity In Rubidium Vapor
authors: Richard Aguiar Maduro, Riaan P. Schmidt, Mustafa A. Al Khafaji, Craig J. A. Millar, Sphinx J. Svensson, Andrey Surzhykov, Adam Selyem, Sonja Franke-Arnold
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate a pump-probe scheme in which an atomic vapor is optically pumped with circularly polarized light and probed with a vector vortex beam. The pump induces a macroscopic magnetization in the medium, which gives rise to frequency-dependent circular dichroism and birefringence. The vortex probe, characterized by spatially varying polarization, maps this optical activity onto the spatial structure of the transmitted light, thereby generating correlations between the frequency, polarization, and spatial degrees of freedom. Measuring the intensity profile in a suitable polarization component then allows us to perform spatially resolved polarization spectroscopy. We demonstrate the translation of frequency shifts into an image rotation, observing on resonance a rotation in the order of 98 mrad per MHz. These findings may find applications in high-precision spectroscopy, magnetometry, and the generation of hybrid entanglement.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a pump-probe scheme in rubidium vapor that creates spatio-spectral vector light with frequency-dependent optical activity, enabling spatially resolved polarization spectroscopy.
motivation: To explore correlations between frequency, polarization, and spatial degrees of light using atomic vapor, with potential applications in spectroscopy and magnetometry.
method: A pump-probe setup: circularly polarized pump induces magnetization in Rb vapor, causing circular dichroism and birefringence; a vector vortex probe maps this activity onto spatial structure.
result: Frequency shifts are translated into image rotation (98 mrad/MHz on resonance), demonstrating spatially resolved polarization spectroscopy.
conclusion: The technique may enable high-precision spectroscopy, magnetometry, and generation of hybrid entanglement, but direct relevance to the user's interests is limited.

title: Sparse Contextual Coupling Reshapes Diffusion Geometry In Multilayer Hypergraphs
authors: Sanjukta Krishnagopal Hao Ding
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many complex systems combine dense background structure with sparse contextual information. We introduce a diffusion-based framework for analyzing how sparse condition-specific layers reshape diffusion geometry in multilayer hypergraphs. Each layer is represented as a weighted hypergraph, layers are coupled through shared entities, and random walks on the coupled system induce multiscale diffusion distances between nodes. We apply the framework to disease-conditioned gene networks by coupling a dense MSigDB functional gene-set layer to sparse disease-specific DGIdb drug-gene hypergraphs, with disease-associated drugs selected from DDDB and HumanNet-GSP used to define external gene weights. Across Bipolar Disorder, Schizophrenia, Leukemia, and Breast Cancer, the disease-specific layer contains less than 2 percent of genes in the coupled system, yet substantially changes diffusion distances and community structure. Centrality analysis suggests that this disproportionate effect arises because DGIdb-associated genes occupy influential positions in the MSigDB-derived functional network. The resulting diffusion-derived communities are stable under subsampling and show coherent post hoc functional enrichment, including signaling and neurotransmission categories in neuropsychiatric diseases and immune, translational, and metabolic categories in cancer-associated diseases. Community-level comparisons further reveal disease similarities not reducible to direct DGIdb gene overlap, including a Breast Cancer-Schizophrenia relationship consistent with recent biomedical evidence. These results show that sparse contextual layers can induce interpretable nonlocal changes in higher-order network geometry.
tldr: This paper introduces a diffusion-based framework for analyzing how sparse contextual layers reshape diffusion geometry in multilayer hypergraphs, applied to disease-conditioned gene networks.
motivation: To understand how sparse condition-specific information can disproportionately affect the geometry and community structure of complex multilayer networks.
method: The authors model each layer as a weighted hypergraph, couple layers through shared entities, and use random walks to compute multiscale diffusion distances. They apply this to gene networks by coupling a dense functional gene-set layer with sparse disease-specific drug-gene hypergraphs.
result: The sparse disease-specific layer (less than 2% of genes) substantially changes diffusion distances and community structure, with disease-associated genes occupying influential positions in the functional network. Communities are stable and show coherent functional enrichment.
conclusion: Sparse contextual layers can induce interpretable nonlocal changes in higher-order network geometry, revealing disease similarities not captured by direct gene overlap.

title: One-Dimensional Nonlinear Quantum Walks
authors: Thomas G. Wong Yujia Shi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore a continuous-time quantum walk starting at a single vertex on the discrete path and cycle with a cubic nonlinearity. Such nonlinearities arise in Bose-Einstein condensates described by the Gross-Pitaevskii equation or by nonlinear optical waveguide arrays. We analytically prove that the nonlinear quantum walk can be trapped to arbitrary fidelity depending on the coefficient of the nonlinear term. This contrasts with linear quantum walks, which are known for spreading quickly in one dimension. We propose that this trapping can be used for timing in quantum state transfer, where a qubit is held at a node until it is ready to be transferred, and it can also be held again at the receiving node. This scheme can also be interpreted as a form of quantum memory, with the trap and transfer corresponding to the storage and release of quantum information.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time quantum walks with cubic nonlinearity on one-dimensional graphs, showing that nonlinearity can trap the walker, enabling timing and memory applications.
motivation: To understand the effect of nonlinearity on quantum walks, which arise in Bose-Einstein condensates and nonlinear optics, and to explore potential applications in quantum state transfer and memory.
method: Analytical proofs and numerical simulations of continuous-time quantum walks on path and cycle graphs with a cubic nonlinear term added to the Schrödinger equation.
result: The nonlinear quantum walk can be trapped to arbitrary fidelity depending on the nonlinear coefficient, contrasting with linear walks that spread quickly.
conclusion: The trapping effect can be used for timing in quantum state transfer and as a form of quantum memory, but the paper does not address energy consumption or entanglement aspects relevant to the user's interests.

title: Ultrafast Excitation Of Bloch Plasmon Polaritons In Hyperbolic Metamaterials With An Extreme Ultra-violet Transient Grating
authors: Tlek Tapani, Hannes Kempf, Matteo Pancaldi, Laura Foglia, Emanuele Pedersoli, Roberta Totani, Adriana Valerio, Riccardo Mincigrucci, Ivaylo Nikolov, Miltcho B. Danailov, Aitor de Andr\'es, Roman Krahne, Paolo Vavassori, Filippo Bencivenga, Flavio Capotondi, Denis Garoli, Nicol\`o Maccaferri
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Manipulating materials properties with light drives advances in materials science and photonics. Hyperbolic metamaterials are promising candidates as next-generation quantum optical media. They support Bloch plasmon polaritons, which are characterized by potentially infinite wave-vectors and long lifetimes, but cannot be excited through direct light illumination due to momentum mismatch. Here, we experimentally show that a transient grating, formed via interference of fully coherent seeded free-electron laser pulses in a thin insulator film, enables the excitation of Bloch plasmon polaritons in an underlying hyperbolic metamaterial. Finite element simulations confirm the role of the transient grating in facilitating phase-matching and mode excitation. Our findings demonstrate a route to spatiotemporally excite Bloch plasmon polaritons modes, offering an alternative to permanently nanostructured gratings and potentially enabling ultrafast control of optical modes excitation.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ultrafast excitation of Bloch plasmon polaritons in hyperbolic metamaterials using a transient grating formed by extreme ultraviolet free-electron laser pulses.
motivation: To overcome the momentum mismatch that prevents direct optical excitation of Bloch plasmon polaritons in hyperbolic metamaterials, which are promising for quantum optical applications.
method: A transient grating is created via interference of fully coherent seeded free-electron laser pulses in a thin insulator film, enabling phase-matching to excite Bloch plasmon polaritons in the underlying hyperbolic metamaterial. Finite element simulations confirm the mechanism.
result: Experimental observation of Bloch plasmon polariton excitation via transient grating, validated by simulations showing the role of the grating in phase-matching.
conclusion: This approach offers an alternative to permanently nanostructured gratings and enables ultrafast spatiotemporal control of optical mode excitation, potentially advancing quantum optical media.

title: Engineering Hybrid Resonances In Nanophotonics
authors: Shutao Zhang, Cheng-Feng Pan, Yandong Fan, Jehyeon Shin, Yuanda Liu, Yan Liu, Jun Ding, Jing Wu, Junsuk Rho, Yuri Kivshar, Joel K. W. Yang, Zhaogang Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybridization of resonances is known to overcome inherent limitations of individual systems, enabling advanced functionalities and applications. Here we discuss hybrid plasmonic-Mie resonators that emerged recently as a promising direction in advancing nanophotonic structures by synergistically combining the strong near-field enhancement of plasmonic components with the low-loss, multipolar resonances of dielectric Mie elements. We review the recent progress in the field, encompassing the fundamental physical principles, structural design strategies, material platforms, computational optimization approaches, and representative device implementations. Our discussion starts by evaluating the complementary characteristics of plasmonic and Mie resonances followed by a description of the coupling between these resonances in order to boost light-matter interactions. Afterward, we explore the performance of efficient hybrid resonators for different application areas. Apart from the conventional metal-dielectric systems, we consider the recent class of epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) materials, which can provide unique advantages in terms of field localization, phase engineering, and energy flow management in the vicinity of zero-permittivity conditions, offering more flexibility in designing hybrid nano-optical devices. Lastly, we point out potential research avenues aiming to improve functional and efficient nanophotonic devices, especially those involving emerging topological material systems, such as Sb2Te3, Bi2Te3, Bi2Se3, combining plasmonic amplification, dielectric confinement, and spin-dependent optical behavior.
tldr: This paper reviews hybrid plasmonic-Mie resonators in nanophotonics, combining plasmonic and dielectric resonances for enhanced light-matter interactions.
motivation: To overcome limitations of individual plasmonic or dielectric resonators by hybridizing them, enabling advanced nanophotonic functionalities.
method: Review of fundamental physics, design strategies, material platforms, computational optimization, and device implementations for hybrid plasmonic-Mie resonators.
result: Hybrid resonators synergistically combine strong near-field enhancement of plasmonics with low-loss multipolar resonances of dielectrics, improving light-matter interactions; epsilon-near-zero materials offer additional flexibility.
conclusion: Future directions include topological materials like Sb2Te3, Bi2Te3, Bi2Se3 for spin-dependent optical behavior and further device optimization.

title: Probing Lattice Dynamics In Real-Space And Real-Time
authors: Navdeep Rana
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The coherent lattice vibrations significantly impact physical and chemical processes in solids, such as heat transfer, displacive phase transitions, and thermal conductivity. Thus, probing lattice dynamics in real-space and real-time is essential for understanding ubiquitous phenomena in solids. High-harmonic spectroscopy (HHS) has emerged as a preferred technique for investigating static and dynamic properties of solids on ultrafast timescales. Yet, despite these accomplishments, the applicability of HHS to probe the influence of coherent lattice vibrations on electronic responses has remained unexplored. In this thesis, we explore the impact of coherent lattice dynamics on attosecond electronic responses in solids using HHS. We observe that coherent excitation of the in-plane phonon mode in graphene results in sidebands in the harmonic spectrum, separated by the frequency of the excited phonon mode. Additionally, we demonstrate the capability of HHS to characterize energy, polarization, phase difference, and the "chirality" of phonon modes. This thesis offers an avenue to probe phonon-driven processes in solids with sub-cycle temporal resolution. In the later segment, our focus shifts toward probing coherent lattice dynamics in real-space and real-time. We demonstrate that inelastic scattering techniques, combined with theoretical analysis, yield comparable results to those from time-resolved diffraction and imaging measurements within pump-probe configurations. Our findings exhibit excellent agreement with results from a time-resolved diffuse x-ray scattering experiment. Our proposed method serves as an alternative to time-resolved diffraction and imaging methods for probing lattice dynamics in real-space and real-time with atomic-scale spatiotemporal resolution.
tldr: This thesis uses high-harmonic spectroscopy and inelastic scattering to probe coherent lattice dynamics in solids with ultrafast temporal resolution.
motivation: To understand the impact of coherent lattice vibrations on electronic responses and to develop methods for probing lattice dynamics in real-space and real-time.
method: High-harmonic spectroscopy (HHS) on graphene with coherent phonon excitation, and inelastic scattering combined with theoretical analysis.
result: Coherent phonon excitation produces sidebands in harmonic spectra; HHS can characterize phonon energy, polarization, phase, and chirality. Inelastic scattering yields results comparable to time-resolved diffraction.
conclusion: HHS and inelastic scattering are effective for probing phonon-driven processes with sub-cycle resolution, offering alternatives to traditional pump-probe methods.

title: Pubo Formulation For Mst And Application To Optimum-Path Forest
authors: Guilherme E. L. Pexe, Lucas A. M. Rattighieri, Leandro A. Passos, Danilo S. Jodas, Douglas Rodrigues, Felipe F. Fanchini, Jo\~ao P. Papa, Kelton A. P. Costa
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Optimum-Path Forest is a graph-based framework for designing classifiers that exploit inter-sample connectivity. A particular variant constructs decision boundaries based on prototypes computed by a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) over the training data, which might become prohibitive for large-scale datasets. In this context, Quantum Machine Learning has emerged as a promising approach to overcome the high computational burden of combinatorial problems. We propose a quantum-inspired approach for prototype selection in OPF classifiers by reformulating the MST problem as a Polynomial Unconstrained Binary Optimization (PUBO) task and further employing the Feedback-Based Quantum Optimization (FALQON) algorithm for Hamiltonian minimization. The PUBO formulation reduces the need for qubits and eliminates the need for auxiliary variables, thereby addressing scalability constraints in current quantum hardware. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that the FALQON-optimized MST achieves accuracies comparable to those of the classical Prim's algorithm while maintaining prototype quality. While FALQON occasionally reached local minima, it did not significantly impact the accuracy of the prototype selection process.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum-inspired PUBO formulation for Minimum Spanning Tree to improve prototype selection in Optimum-Path Forest classifiers, using FALQON for optimization.
motivation: To address the computational burden of MST-based prototype selection in large-scale datasets for OPF classifiers.
method: Reformulates MST as a Polynomial Unconstrained Binary Optimization (PUBO) problem and applies the Feedback-Based Quantum Optimization (FALQON) algorithm to minimize the Hamiltonian.
result: FALQON-optimized MST achieves accuracies comparable to classical Prim's algorithm on real-world datasets, though it occasionally gets stuck in local minima without significantly affecting prototype quality.
conclusion: The PUBO formulation reduces qubit requirements and eliminates auxiliary variables, showing promise for near-term quantum devices, but the work is primarily in quantum machine learning for classification, not directly related to the user's interests.

title: Entanglement Growth From Structured Initial States In Many-Body Localized Systems
authors: Pengfei Zhang Chen Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how complex entanglement structures emerge is a central problem in quantum many-body physics. Recent work by Zhang et al. has considered structured initial states prepared by evolving a product state under a chaotic Hamiltonian for a finite time before quenching to the target Hamiltonian. In this setup, total entanglement entropy growth in many-body localized systems exhibits two distinct regimes, first increasing and then decreasing as the initial entanglement is tuned. In this work, we identify the physical origin of this behavior by analyzing the dynamics of both the R\'enyi entanglement entropy and the Wehrl-R\'enyi entropy in the random-field XXZ model, the latter of which characterizes multipartite entanglement. We show that a similar non-monotonic dependence on the initial entanglement also appears in the net growth of the Wehrl-R\'enyi entropy for product states polarized along the [MATH]-direction. The first regime is governed by a finite magnetization associated with local integrals of motion, while the second reflects inter-site correlations. In contrast, for product states in the [MATH]-direction, the entanglement growth exhibits a monotonic decay. Our results provide a more fine-grained picture of how distinct initial-state properties shape entanglement dynamics in many-body localized systems.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement growth in many-body localized systems from structured initial states, revealing non-monotonic behavior depending on initial state magnetization.
motivation: To understand how complex entanglement structures emerge in quantum many-body systems, specifically the effect of structured initial states on entanglement dynamics in many-body localized systems.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of Rényi entanglement entropy and Wehrl-Rényi entropy in the random-field XXZ model, comparing product states polarized along different directions.
result: They find non-monotonic dependence of entanglement growth on initial entanglement for certain initial states, governed by magnetization and inter-site correlations, while other states show monotonic decay.
conclusion: The results provide a fine-grained picture of how initial-state properties shape entanglement dynamics in many-body localized systems, but the paper does not directly address the user's research interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, quantum communication, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Mid-infrared Single-photon Sub-pixel Temporal Ghost Imaging
authors: Wen Zhang, Kun Huang, Zhibin Zhao, Huijie Ma, Ziyu He, Jianan Fang, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temporal ghost imaging (TGI) enables ultrafast temporal signal recovery using slow detectors, offering a promising route for high-speed mid-infrared (MIR) detection. However, conventional schemes remain limited in temporal resolution by the modulation bandwidth or pattern timescale, and are mostly confined to structured illumination. Here, we demonstrated a high-resolution MIR single-photon computational TGI system, which integrated nonlinear structured detection with sub-pixel temporal shifting. A pre-programmed near-infrared pump serves as a temporally optical gate to drive sum-frequency generation in a nonlinear crystal. Consequently, MIR waveforms at 3.4 [MATH]m were upconverted, and captured by a room-temperature silicon detector. We realized sub-pixel operation by fractional-bin temporal stepping of the gate and multi-shot fusion via pseudo-inverse reconstruction. The sub-pixel shifting strategy decouples the achievable resolution from modulation speed, enabling 40 ps temporal precision at a driving rate of only 3.125 Gbps. This performance surpasses both detector jitter and pattern-rate limits, while maintaining single-photon sensitivity. The presented paradigm establishes a versatile route for ultrafast MIR waveform reconstruction, opening new opportunities in high-resolution infrared sensing and quantum photonics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a mid-infrared single-photon temporal ghost imaging system with sub-pixel temporal resolution using nonlinear upconversion and computational reconstruction.
motivation: To overcome the temporal resolution limitations of conventional temporal ghost imaging, which are constrained by modulation bandwidth and pattern timescale, and to enable high-speed mid-infrared detection with slow detectors.
method: A pre-programmed near-infrared pump serves as a temporal optical gate for sum-frequency generation in a nonlinear crystal, upconverting MIR waveforms to be captured by a room-temperature silicon detector. Sub-pixel temporal shifting is achieved by fractional-bin stepping of the gate and multi-shot fusion via pseudo-inverse reconstruction.
result: The system achieves 40 ps temporal precision at a driving rate of only 3.125 Gbps, surpassing both detector jitter and pattern-rate limits while maintaining single-photon sensitivity.
conclusion: This paradigm establishes a versatile route for ultrafast MIR waveform reconstruction, opening new opportunities in high-resolution infrared sensing and quantum photonics.

title: Generalized Quantum Stein's Lemma For Mixed Sources
authors: Hayata Yamasaki Haruka Kanazawa
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The generalized quantum Stein's lemma characterizes the optimal asymptotic exponent of the type-II error in quantum hypothesis testing for an independent and identically distributed (IID) null hypothesis against a composite alternative hypothesis. Classically, a probabilistic mixture of IID sources arises as a natural generalization of IID sources, and, in the non-composite setting, the optimal type-II error exponent in hypothesis testing for such classical mixed sources is known to be characterized concisely by the worst-case component of the mixture. In this work, we extend these foundational results to composite quantum hypothesis testing where the null hypothesis is a mixed source, i.e., a probabilistic mixture of IID quantum states, and the alternative hypothesis is composite as in the generalized quantum Stein's lemma. When the type-I error vanishes asymptotically, we characterize the optimal type-II error exponent of this composite quantum hypothesis testing problem in terms of the worst-case component of the mixture, by developing techniques for the non-commutative quantum setting inspired by the classical information-spectrum analysis. We also show that the analogous characterization does not hold in general for a fixed nonzero type-I error threshold, by providing a counterexample beyond the vanishing type-I error regime. These results clarify the applicability of the generalized quantum Stein's lemma to highly non-IID null hypotheses arising from arbitrary finite probabilistic mixtures of IID quantum states.
tldr: This paper extends the generalized quantum Stein's lemma to composite hypothesis testing with mixed IID sources, characterizing the optimal type-II error exponent in the vanishing type-I error regime.
motivation: To understand the asymptotic error exponents in quantum hypothesis testing when the null hypothesis is a probabilistic mixture of IID states, which is a natural generalization of IID sources.
method: The authors develop techniques inspired by classical information-spectrum analysis for the non-commutative quantum setting to handle composite alternative hypotheses.
result: The optimal type-II error exponent is given by the worst-case component of the mixture when type-I error vanishes, but this characterization fails for fixed nonzero type-I error thresholds.
conclusion: The results clarify the applicability of the generalized quantum Stein's lemma to non-IID null hypotheses arising from finite mixtures of IID states, with implications for quantum hypothesis testing theory.

title: Circuits Of Quantum Hashing And Quantum Fourier Transform For A Cactus As A Qubit Connectivity Graph
authors: Ilnur Valeev Kamil Khadiev
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a quantum circuit implementation of the quantum hashing algorithm (quantum fingerprinting) for a quantum device with restrictions on the application of two-qubit gates by a qubit connectivity graph. We present an optimization technique for the shallow circuit for quantum hashing in the case of a cactus as a qubit connectivity graph. The algorithm has [MATH] complexity to build the circuit, where [MATH] is the number of qubits and [MATH] is the number of connections (edges) in the graph. It is improvement compared to the existing exponential-time algorithm in the case of arbitrary graphs. The algorithm uses solution for the shortest non-simple 1-covering path problem as a subroutine. We present an [MATH]-time solution for this graph-theory problem in the case of a cactus. This result can be interesting independently. The algorithm also used for improving of the quantum circuit for Quantum Fourier Transform.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum circuit implementation of quantum hashing optimized for a cactus qubit connectivity graph, with applications to quantum Fourier transform.
motivation: To enable quantum hashing on near-term quantum devices with limited qubit connectivity, and to improve circuit depth for specific graph topologies.
method: The authors develop an optimization technique for shallow quantum hashing circuits on cactus graphs, using a polynomial-time solution for the shortest non-simple 1-covering path problem.
result: The algorithm achieves polynomial complexity O(n^2 + m) for building the circuit, improving over exponential-time algorithms for arbitrary graphs.
conclusion: The work provides a practical circuit construction for quantum hashing on restricted connectivity, with potential extensions to other graph families and quantum Fourier transform optimization.

title: Towards Compact High-frequency Nonreciprocal Devices Using Nanoplasma-switched Time-varying Metasurfaces
authors: Mikhail Sidorenko, Jin Zhang, Xuchen Wang, Zhipei Sun, Sergei Tretyakov, Viktar Asadchy
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-modulated systems have received growing interest in recent years. They allow us to tailor effects, such as frequency conversion, single-direction propagation, etc. For the microwave band, semiconductor elements, such as varactors, are usually used as time-modulated elements but their modulation frequency has been limited to the few-gigahertz range. Recent advances in nanoplasma switches, i.e., two-state electronic switches based on a gas discharge in a nanometer-scale gap, provide a new potential for developing time-modulated systems with high operating frequencies. Here, we develop an analytical framework based on the time-Floquet method for the design of nonreciprocal time-modulated devices based on two-state time-modulated elements, for instance, nanoplasma-based switches. A practical example of a microwave isolator operating at 100~GHz frequency is developed and studied both analytically and using full-wave simulations. A potential realization in a parallel-plate waveguide is also simulated numerically.
tldr: This paper presents an analytical framework for designing high-frequency nonreciprocal devices using nanoplasma-switched time-varying metasurfaces, with a demonstration at 100 GHz.
motivation: To overcome the modulation frequency limitations of conventional semiconductor-based time-modulated elements (e.g., varactors) and enable nonreciprocal devices at higher frequencies (e.g., 100 GHz).
method: Develops a time-Floquet analytical framework for two-state time-modulated elements (nanoplasma switches) and validates it with full-wave simulations and a parallel-plate waveguide realization.
result: A microwave isolator operating at 100 GHz is designed and analyzed, showing nonreciprocal behavior enabled by nanoplasma switches.
conclusion: Nanoplasma switches offer a promising path for compact, high-frequency nonreciprocal devices, with potential applications in communication and radar systems.

title: A Maxwell Quadratic-Form Representation Of The Parallel-Plate Casimir Trace From Codimension-Three Riesz Reduction
authors: Bilal Khan Irshadullah Khan
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a Maxwell version of the codimension-three Riesz/Gaussian quadratic-form representation for perfectly conducting parallel plates. This paper is the Maxwell follow-up to the scalar codimension-three Riesz/Gaussian representation theorem presented earlier in arXiv:2605.06693(2026): the same transverse Riesz reduction and prescribed-covariance quadratic-form mechanism are carried over here to the physical parallel-plate Maxwell operator. The construction is carried out in finite lateral volume [MATH], using the physical electric-field Hilbert space of divergence-free fields satisfying the perfect-conductor tangential condition [MATH], with the static normal zero mode removed. The Maxwell curl-curl operator is defined by its closed quadratic form, and an explicit Fourier-domain analysis proves the finite-volume spectral gap, compact resolvent, and heat-trace admissibility needed for the stochastic construction. For this reduced Maxwell operator [MATH], the codimension-three Riesz integral gives the transversely reduced Riesz mediator [MATH]. A prescribed heat-regularized Gaussian source with covariance [MATH] then has expected quadratic Green energy equal to the heat-regularized physical Maxwell trace. The finite-volume trace is shown to be spectrally equivalent to a scalar Dirichlet channel plus a scalar Neumann channel with its constant zero mode removed. Under the standard parallel-plate interaction finite-part prescription, the large-area energy density is $[MATH]$ The result is a representation theorem for the Maxwell parallel-plate trace under a prescribed covariance in the flat-plate geometry considered here.
tldr: This paper develops a Maxwell quadratic-form representation for the parallel-plate Casimir trace using codimension-three Riesz reduction, extending a scalar result to the electromagnetic field.
motivation: To provide a rigorous stochastic representation for the Casimir energy of parallel plates in quantum electrodynamics, building on previous scalar work.
method: The authors use codimension-three Riesz/Gaussian quadratic-form representation, Fourier-domain analysis, and spectral theory to define the Maxwell curl-curl operator with perfect conductor boundary conditions.
result: They show the finite-volume trace is spectrally equivalent to a scalar Dirichlet channel plus a scalar Neumann channel with constant zero mode removed, and derive the large-area energy density.
conclusion: The work establishes a representation theorem for the Maxwell parallel-plate trace under prescribed covariance, but its direct relevance to the user's interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, communication, or hybrid systems is limited.

title: Super-Beamforming In Holographic Mimo
authors: Angel Lozano Andrea Pizzo
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The conventional linear scaling of beamforming gain with the number of antennas is not a fundamental physical limitation, but rather a consequence of the half-wavelength spacings that minimize mutual coupling. Relaxing this constraint facilitates beamforming gains exceeding those of uncoupled arrays along specific directions. This paper shows that, when antenna losses remain sufficiently small, mutual coupling enables the synthesis of super-beams whose endfire gain scales quadratically with the number of antennas. Notably, this quadratic scaling does not necessarily require vanishing spacings, but emerges for spacings slightly below half wavelength as the array aperture increases.
tldr: This paper shows that mutual coupling in antenna arrays can enable super-beamforming with quadratic gain scaling, challenging the conventional linear scaling limit.
motivation: To explore whether beamforming gain can exceed the conventional linear scaling with number of antennas by relaxing the half-wavelength spacing constraint.
method: Theoretical analysis of mutual coupling effects in antenna arrays, deriving scaling laws for endfire gain under non-vanishing spacings.
result: Endfire gain can scale quadratically with the number of antennas when antenna losses are small, even for spacings slightly below half wavelength.
conclusion: Mutual coupling can be harnessed to achieve super-beamforming, with implications for holographic MIMO and array design.

title: A Simple GPU-Accelerated Solver For The Schr\"odinger Operator With Applications To Ground States And Hamiltonian Simulation
authors: Xiangxiong Zhang Xinyu Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the tensor-product direct solver from the Laplacian to the Schr\"odinger operator [MATH]. When the potential [MATH] is separable, the operator [MATH] is inverted or exponentiated at cost [MATH] in [MATH] dimensions via per-axis eigendecomposition. On a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, this costs less than one second for [MATH] degrees of freedom in 3D. For non-separable potentials [MATH], the same solver provides a preconditioner [MATH] for the preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) method and a propagator for operator-splitting time integrators. For bounded [MATH], we prove that the preconditioned operator has a bounded condition number and a clustered spectrum with at most finitely many outlier eigenvalues, independently of the mesh size, and also independently of the domain size when [MATH] is a confining potential. This explains the mesh- and domain-independent PCG iteration counts observed in practice. We apply this method to ground state computation via inverse iteration for linear problems and via the [MATH] gradient flow for Gross--Pitaevskii energy in 3D, and also Hamiltonian simulation via the approximated qHOP and Magnus-2 splitting methods from 3D to 9D on a single NVIDIA GH200 GPU.
tldr: This paper presents a GPU-accelerated solver for the Schrödinger operator, focusing on ground state computation and Hamiltonian simulation, but does not directly address the user's research interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, quantum communication, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To develop efficient numerical methods for solving the Schrödinger equation in high dimensions, which is computationally challenging.
method: Extends a tensor-product direct solver from the Laplacian to the Schrödinger operator, using per-axis eigendecomposition for separable potentials and preconditioned conjugate gradient for non-separable potentials, with GPU acceleration.
result: The solver achieves low cost for separable potentials and mesh-independent iteration counts for non-separable potentials; demonstrated on ground state computation and Hamiltonian simulation up to 9D.
conclusion: The method provides a practical tool for quantum simulations, but its relevance to the user's specific research areas is limited.

title: Partially Observable Restless Bandits For Age-Optimal Scheduling Over Markov Channels
authors: Xijun Wang, Shuying Gan, Yanzhi Huang, Xiaoyu Zhao, Chao Xu, Xiang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There is a surge of need for fresh information with the overwhelming proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) applications. To characterize the information freshness perceived by the destination, the age of information (AoI) has been proposed. In this paper, we consider an IoT system with multiple devices sending status update packets to a central controller through time-correlated Markov channels and assume that the instantaneous channel states are not available to the central controller before making scheduling decisions. To ensure information freshness, we investigate a timely scheduling problem that minimizes the total expected time-average AoI under a strict communications bandwidth constraint. We formulate this problem as a partially observable restless multi-armed bandit problem. Using Lagrangian relaxation, we decouple the relaxed problem into multiple sub-problems and prove the threshold structure of their optimal policies. Armed with this property, we establish the indexability for the decoupled problem and design an algorithm to compute the Whittle's index. To reduce implementation complexity, we further derive the Whittle-like index in closed-form for low-complexity scheduling. Simulation results show that the proposed index-based policies outperform the baselines, remain close to the optimal policy or relaxed lower bound, and are especially effective when scheduling resources are limited or the network size is large.
tldr: This paper studies age-optimal scheduling over Markov channels using partially observable restless bandits, with no direct connection to the user's research interests.
motivation: To minimize age of information (AoI) in IoT systems with time-correlated channels and limited bandwidth.
method: Formulates as a partially observable restless multi-armed bandit, uses Lagrangian relaxation, proves threshold structure, and computes Whittle's index.
result: Proposed index-based policies outperform baselines and approach optimal or relaxed lower bound, especially under limited resources.
conclusion: The work provides efficient scheduling policies for AoI minimization, but is not aligned with the user's focus on quantum information, thermodynamics, or foundations.

title: Information Leakage Envelopes
authors: Sara Saeidian (KTH Royal Institute Of Technology, Inria Saclay), Carlos Pinz\'on (inria Saclay, \'ecole Polytechnique), Catuscia Palamidessi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study privacy guarantees in the framework of pointwise maximal leakage (PML) that satisfy two requirements: they are robust under post-processing and upper bound the failure probability, i.e., the probability that the information leakage exceeds a given threshold. We first examine two candidate definitions inspired by (approximate) differential privacy and show that neither one satisfies both requirements simultaneously. We then introduce the notion of the PML envelope, which quantifies the largest amount of information leakage about a secret after arbitrary post-processing of a mechanism's output. By construction, the PML envelope satisfies both requirements. We discuss basic structural properties of the envelope, such as monotonicity, and derive general upper and lower bounds. We further analyze the envelope for two widely used privacy mechanisms: the PML-extremal mechanisms in the high-privacy regime and randomized response. Overall, this work establishes the PML envelope as a natural and operationally meaningful definition for providing privacy guarantees that are preserved under arbitrary downstream transformations.
tldr: This paper introduces the PML envelope, a privacy guarantee that is robust under post-processing and bounds failure probability, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests.
motivation: To define privacy guarantees that are preserved under arbitrary post-processing and can upper bound the probability of leakage exceeding a threshold.
method: The authors examine candidate definitions from differential privacy, then propose the PML envelope and analyze its properties and bounds for specific mechanisms.
result: The PML envelope satisfies both robustness under post-processing and failure probability bounding, unlike the candidate definitions.
conclusion: The PML envelope provides a natural and operationally meaningful privacy definition, with potential applications in privacy-preserving data analysis.

title: Local Circular Dichroism And Polarization Coupling In Phthalocyanine Molecular Assemblies Revealed By Photoinduced Force Microscopy
authors: Masayoshi Fujii, Mamoru Tamura, Hidemasa Yamane, Hajime Ishihara
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photoinduced force microscopy (PiFM) enables nanoscale visualization of optical responses by directly detecting photoinduced forces without relying on luminescence. In molecular assemblies, intermolecular polarization coupling can generate collective excitation modes and chiral optical responses that are absent in isolated molecules. In this study, we theoretically investigate PiFM images of ZnPc molecular assemblies using the discrete dipole approximation combined with nonlocal molecular susceptibilities. Under linearly polarized illumination, bonding and antibonding polarization-coupling modes are found to produce characteristic spatial distributions in both the optical force spectra and PiFM images of molecular dimers and tetramers. Furthermore, under circularly polarized illumination, intermolecular coupling and asymmetric molecular packing generate enhanced local circular dichroism distributions characterized by large asymmetric factors and spatially varying chiral contrasts. These results demonstrate that PiFM can spatially resolve collective polarization modes and local chiral optical responses in molecular assemblies, providing insight into nanoscale intermolecular optical interactions.
tldr: This paper uses photoinduced force microscopy to study local circular dichroism and polarization coupling in phthalocyanine molecular assemblies, focusing on nanoscale optical responses.
motivation: To understand how intermolecular polarization coupling generates collective excitation modes and chiral optical responses in molecular assemblies, which are absent in isolated molecules.
method: Theoretical investigation using discrete dipole approximation combined with nonlocal molecular susceptibilities to simulate PiFM images of ZnPc molecular dimers and tetramers.
result: Bonding and antibonding polarization-coupling modes produce characteristic spatial distributions in optical force spectra and PiFM images; circularly polarized illumination reveals enhanced local circular dichroism with large asymmetric factors and spatially varying chiral contrasts.
conclusion: PiFM can spatially resolve collective polarization modes and local chiral optical responses, providing insight into nanoscale intermolecular optical interactions.

title: Brascamp--Lieb Inequalities For Fractal Dimensions
authors: Jonathan M. Fraser
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use the Brascamp--Lieb inequality from functional analysis to prove novel inequalities for the upper box, packing, and Assouad dimensions of fractal sets in terms of the dimensions of certain projections. Analogous inequalities do not hold for Hausdorff or lower box dimensions. We apply these fractal Brascamp--Lieb inequalities to establish new exceptional set estimates for orthogonal projections and to provide sharp dimension estimates for certain constrained sumsets. We also establish analogous nonlinear inequalities via the nonlinear Brascamp--Lieb inequality.
tldr: This paper uses Brascamp-Lieb inequalities to derive new inequalities for fractal dimensions of projections, with applications to exceptional set estimates and constrained sumsets.
motivation: To extend Brascamp-Lieb inequalities from functional analysis to fractal geometry, providing new tools for understanding dimensions of projections and related problems.
method: The authors apply the Brascamp-Lieb inequality to upper box, packing, and Assouad dimensions, and also use a nonlinear version for nonlinear settings.
result: They prove novel inequalities for these fractal dimensions in terms of projection dimensions, which do not hold for Hausdorff or lower box dimensions, and establish new exceptional set estimates and sharp dimension estimates for constrained sumsets.
conclusion: The work opens new connections between functional analysis and fractal geometry, with potential applications in geometric measure theory and related fields.

title: Design And Fabrication Of Coaxial Dual Core Optical Fiber Fan-in Device
authors: Yuhong Ma, Shitai Yang, Libo Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid development of information and communication technologies in recent years, the transmission capacity of single-core optical fibers has nearly reached its physical limit. Space-division multiplexing based on multi-core fibers offers an effective solution to this bottleneck. Multi-core fibers feature high integration and large transmission capacity, and their unique structural characteristics also give them special value in fiber-optic sensing applications. Among various types of multi-core fibers, coaxial dual-core fibers (CDCFs) have shown promising performance in particle trapping, signal emission, and spectral analysis. To enable reliable interconnection between different types of multi-core fibers and single-core fiber arrays, this paper presents the design and fabrication of a fan-in device for coaxial dual-core fibers with different core diameters. The proposed method relies solely on cold-processing techniques and does not require any fusion splicing or thermal processing. The device is implemented on a V-groove substrate. Through structural design, fabrication, and experimental characterization, the average insertion loss of the ring core and the central core at a wavelength of 980 nm is measured to be 2.15 dB and 1.25 dB, respectively, demonstrating the successful fabrication of a coaxial dual-core fan-in device.
tldr: This paper presents the design and fabrication of a coaxial dual-core fiber fan-in device using cold-processing techniques.
motivation: To address the capacity limit of single-core fibers and enable reliable interconnection between multi-core fibers and single-core fiber arrays.
method: The fan-in device is fabricated on a V-groove substrate using only cold-processing techniques, avoiding fusion splicing or thermal processing.
result: Average insertion losses of 2.15 dB for the ring core and 1.25 dB for the central core at 980 nm were achieved.
conclusion: The successful fabrication demonstrates a viable approach for coaxial dual-core fiber fan-in devices, with potential applications in space-division multiplexing and sensing.

title: The Securitization Of Science: A Systems Perspective On Policy And Measurement
authors: Caroline S. Wagner
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: International scientific collaboration is organized primarily by researcher-level logic and network dynamics in which scientists seek partners at the frontier of their field with little consideration of national affiliation. Research security policies that raise the friction costs of international collaboration are often assumed to operate against this logic, aiming to produce selective withdrawal from sensitive fields to deny knowledge transfer to specific countries. This paper tests that assumption against eight years of bibliometric evidence from China's scientific output from 2018 through 2025 across 27 Scopus subject categories. China's internationally co-authored publication share declined universally across all fields after 2018, consistent with China's push for domestic capacity maturation, but the pattern of decline is inconsistent with the deterrence prediction. Fields with high dual-use proximity, including computer science, materials science, physics and astronomy, chemical engineering, and engineering, showed the least contraction (3-6 percentage points), while fields with minimal dual-use salience (psychology, nursing, dentistry, and health professions) showed the steepest declines (8-24 percentage points). The findings suggest that governments raised the friction level but did not redirect the network nor suppress collaboration in sensitive areas. Researchers practiced adaptive participation, maintaining frontier collaborations while adjusting the form and language of their engagement. This pattern matches what the invisible college theory and the Ostrom knowledge commons framework predict.
tldr: This paper analyzes international scientific collaboration and security policies using bibliometric data, finding that China's declining co-authorship share is inconsistent with deterrence predictions.
motivation: To test the assumption that research security policies reduce collaboration in sensitive fields, using China's scientific output as a case study.
method: Bibliometric analysis of China's internationally co-authored publications across 27 Scopus subject categories from 2018 to 2025.
result: China's co-authored publication share declined universally, but fields with high dual-use proximity showed the least contraction, contrary to deterrence expectations.
conclusion: Governments raised friction costs but did not redirect networks; scientists adapted by maintaining frontier collaborations while adjusting engagement forms.

title: 2d GaSe-Based Single-Pixel Spectrometer Via Electro-Optical Barrier Co-Modulation
authors: Shibesh Pramanik, Rishabh Sahoo, Arnab Mondal, Tithi Saha, Ankush Bag, Vibhav Bharadwaj Shivakumar, Rishi Maiti
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Driven by the growing demand for miniaturized spectrometers for in-situ analysis, and point-of-care diagnostics, conventional spectrometers are often constrained by bulky architectures and pathlength-limited spectral resolution. Achieving high-resolution, single-pixel computational spectrometers is therefore critical for the realization of compact, on-chip systems. Here, we report a single-pixel spectrometer enabled by a single 2D material; few-layer GaSe-based photodetector, in which the Schottky barrier height modulation, governed jointly by applied bias and optical excitation, provides an efficient mechanism for spectral encoding without the need for bulky dispersive elements. The device exhibits a high peak-wavelength accuracy of ~0.78 nm across a broad operational bandwidth (300-700 nm) within a compact footprint of ~100 um^2 and resolves closely spaced spectral features with separations down to ~5 nm. The device operates at low bias (+/- 4V) with an ultralow dark current density ~0.3 pA/um^2 at 4V bias. These results establish a simple, scalable route toward compact, cost-effective spectroscopic systems for on-chip spectral sensing and portable hyperspectral imaging applications.
tldr: A single-pixel spectrometer using a few-layer GaSe photodetector with bias-optical co-modulation for spectral encoding.
motivation: To overcome the bulkiness and pathlength limitations of conventional spectrometers for compact, on-chip sensing.
method: Schottky barrier height modulation via applied bias and optical excitation in a 2D GaSe photodetector enables spectral encoding without dispersive elements.
result: Achieved ~0.78 nm peak-wavelength accuracy over 300-700 nm, 5 nm spectral resolution, low bias (±4V), and ultralow dark current (~0.3 pA/μm²).
conclusion: Provides a simple, scalable route to compact spectrometers for portable hyperspectral imaging and on-chip sensing.

title: A Bounded-Confidence Model Of Opinion Dynamics With Adaptive Interaction Probabilities
authors: Leila Thompsky (yolanda), Yuexuan (yolanda), Wu, Mason A. Porter, Jiajie Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Models of opinion dynamics aim to capture how individuals' opinions change when they interact with each other. One well-known model of opinion dynamics is the Deffuant--Weisbuch (DW) model, which is a type of bounded-confidence model (BCM). In the DW model, agents have pairwise interactions, and they are receptive to other agents' opinions when their opinions are sufficiently close to each other. In this paper, we extend the DW model by studying it on networks with heterogeneous and adaptive edge weights between pairs of agents. These edge weights govern the interaction probabilities between the agents and thereby encode the idea that people are more likely to communicate with individuals with whom they have previously compromised or had other positive interactions. We prove theoretical guarantees of our adaptive edge-weighted DW model's convergence properties, the long-time dynamics of its edge weights, and the model's associated ``effective graph", which is a time-dependent subgraph that includes edges only between agents that are receptive to each other's opinions. We support our theoretical results with numerical simulations of our adaptive edge-weighted DW model on a variety of networks and find that including adaptive edge weights yields different qualitative dynamics for different types of networks. In particular, for small confidence bounds, we observe that incorporating adaptive edge weights decreases the convergence time for dense networks but increases the convergence time for sparse networks.
tldr: This paper extends the Deffuant-Weisbuch bounded-confidence model of opinion dynamics by incorporating adaptive edge weights that reflect interaction probabilities, and analyzes convergence properties and network-dependent dynamics.
motivation: To better model real-world opinion dynamics where individuals are more likely to interact with those they have previously compromised with, and to understand how adaptive interaction probabilities affect consensus formation.
method: The authors propose an adaptive edge-weighted Deffuant-Weisbuch model, prove theoretical convergence guarantees, and perform numerical simulations on various network topologies.
result: Adaptive edge weights decrease convergence time for dense networks but increase it for sparse networks when confidence bounds are small; the effective graph dynamics are characterized.
conclusion: The model captures more realistic opinion dynamics and suggests that network structure and adaptivity significantly influence consensus speed, with implications for social network modeling.

title: Universal Thin-shell Limits For The Viscous Operator On Riemannian Hypersurfaces
authors: Samuel L. Braunstein Zhi-Wei Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We decompose the ambient Bochner Laplacian acting on tangential vector fields on a thin shell around an arbitrary smooth hypersurface [MATH] into an intrinsic piece and a radial boundary-shear piece. The intrinsic piece is the deformation Laplacian [MATH] on every hypersurface, regardless of extrinsic geometry. The boundary-shear piece is determined entirely by the normal profile of the velocity field. We prove that stress-free (Navier slip) boundary conditions yield the deformation Laplacian universally, and that Hodge (zero tangential vorticity) boundary conditions yield the Hodge Laplacian universally. Both results hold on any smooth hypersurface, not only on surfaces of constant curvature. This extends the sphere-specific results of Temam-Ziane and Miura to the general case and explains the extension-dependence found by Chan, Czubak, and Yoneda on the ellipsoid as a physical boundary-condition dependence. We also derive a continuous one-parameter family of boundary conditions interpolating between the two limits, producing an effective viscous operator [MATH] that couples to the extrinsic geometry (through the shape operator squared) only in the intermediate partial-slip regime.
tldr: This paper derives universal thin-shell limits for the viscous operator on Riemannian hypersurfaces, showing that stress-free and Hodge boundary conditions yield the deformation and Hodge Laplacians respectively, independent of extrinsic geometry.
motivation: To generalize previous sphere-specific results to arbitrary smooth hypersurfaces and explain the extension-dependence observed in prior work on ellipsoids.
method: Decomposition of the ambient Bochner Laplacian into intrinsic and radial boundary-shear pieces, followed by analysis of boundary conditions (stress-free, Hodge, and a one-parameter family).
result: Stress-free boundary conditions universally yield the deformation Laplacian; Hodge boundary conditions yield the Hodge Laplacian; a continuous family of boundary conditions produces an effective viscous operator coupling to extrinsic geometry only in the partial-slip regime.
conclusion: The results extend known limits to general hypersurfaces and clarify the role of boundary conditions in viscous operators, with implications for fluid dynamics and geometric analysis.

title: Wide-field Mid-infrared Edge-enhanced Upconversion Imaging
authors: Mengyao Yu, Zhuohang Wei, Jianan Fang, Jixi Zhang, Tingting Zheng, Shina Liao, Kun Huang, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Edge-enhanced imaging is critical for visualizing weakly absorbing and transparent objects. Extending this functionality into the mid-infrared (MIR) region enables chemical sensitivity and improved imaging performance for biomedical, material, and remote-sensing applications. Here, we present a wide-field MIR edge-enhanced upconversion imaging system that integrates vortex-pump complex-amplitude engineering with aperiodic quasi-phase matching. In contrast to the bright-field modality, the wide-field edge-enhanced operation shows sensitive dependence on the crystal position relative to the Fourier plane. The system achieves single-shot operation with a 25-mm field of view and 79-[MATH]m spatial resolution, yielding a record-high space-bandwidth product of [MATH]. We show that this capability enables direct visualization of phase gradients in transparent optical elements and enhances structural contrast in biological specimens. The demonstrated architecture combines high sensitivity, spectral specificity, and robust edge detection, offering a promising route toward advanced MIR imaging in industrial inspection and biomedical diagnostics.
tldr: This paper presents a wide-field mid-infrared edge-enhanced upconversion imaging system using vortex-pump complex-amplitude engineering and aperiodic quasi-phase matching.
motivation: To extend edge-enhanced imaging into the mid-infrared region for chemical sensitivity and improved imaging of weakly absorbing and transparent objects.
method: The system integrates vortex-pump complex-amplitude engineering with aperiodic quasi-phase matching in an upconversion imaging setup.
result: Achieves single-shot operation with a 25-mm field of view, 79-μm spatial resolution, and a record-high space-bandwidth product, enabling direct visualization of phase gradients and enhanced structural contrast.
conclusion: The demonstrated architecture offers high sensitivity, spectral specificity, and robust edge detection, promising for industrial inspection and biomedical diagnostics.

title: Coherent Control Of The Goos-H\"{a}nchen Shift In Otto Structure
authors: Magdi Bajusair, Mohammad H. Alhakami, Saeed Asiri
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate controlling the lateral Goos-H\"{a}nchen (GH) shift for a TM-polarized field reflected from Otto structure containing four level N-type atomic medium. The N-type atomic configuration can be formed by coupling the standard three-level [MATH] system to an additional upper energy level through a coherent driving field. The medium can then be switched from transparent to absorptive under the effect of the driving field. In the Otto structure, an air gap typically separates a dielectric prism from a metal film. We show that the sign and magnitude of the GH shift can be highly controlled when the air gap is replaced by the coherent atomic medium. This can be achieved by adjusting the strength of the applied fields to the atomic medium, while the geometrical characteristics of the proposed structure are unchanged.
tldr: The paper investigates coherent control of the Goos-Hänchen shift in an Otto structure using a four-level N-type atomic medium.
motivation: To achieve tunable control of the lateral Goos-Hänchen shift for TM-polarized light, which has potential applications in optical switching and sensing.
method: The Otto structure is modified by replacing the air gap with a coherently driven four-level N-type atomic medium. The GH shift is analyzed as a function of the driving field strength and other parameters.
result: The sign and magnitude of the GH shift can be highly controlled by adjusting the applied fields to the atomic medium, without changing the geometry of the structure.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a new way to manipulate the GH shift coherently, which may be useful for integrated photonic devices.

title: Scalable Native Signed Optical Computing Enabled By Dual-wavelength Incoherent Multiplexing
authors: Yuan Ren, Yong Zheng, Ruixue Liu, Yunpeng Song, Qinfen Huang, Min Wang, Ya Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Incoherent photonic neural networks (PNNs) provide a robust platform for analog optical computing, yet efficient implementation of native signed operations remains challenging. Existing incoherent PNNs approaches often require additional spatial channels or temporal encoding steps to represent bipolar input signals, resulting in hardware overhead that scales with system size. Here, we demonstrate a dual-wavelength incoherent photonic architecture that natively supports both signed inputs and signed weights on a thin-film lithium niobate platform. By encoding complementary signal components onto two wavelength channels and performing computation within a shared physical path, the proposed scheme eliminates duplicated weighting units. As a result, the additional hardware overhead associated with signed computation remains constant per multiply accumulate operation, independent of matrix size. The fabricated device exhibits a modulation bandwidth exceeding 40 GHz and achieves four-quadrant optical multiplication with a standard deviation error of 1.27%. System-level functionality is validated through neural-network classification, achieving 95.1% accuracy on the Moons dataset and 91.63% on MNIST. These results establish a practical route toward scalable incoherent photonic computing systems with native bipolar processing capability.
tldr: This paper presents a dual-wavelength incoherent photonic architecture for signed optical computing, achieving high-speed modulation and accurate neural network classification.
motivation: Existing incoherent photonic neural networks require extra spatial or temporal resources to handle signed (bipolar) signals, leading to hardware overhead that scales with system size.
method: The authors encode complementary signal components onto two wavelength channels and perform computation in a shared physical path on a thin-film lithium niobate platform, eliminating duplicated weighting units.
result: The device achieves >40 GHz modulation bandwidth, four-quadrant multiplication with 1.27% error, and classification accuracies of 95.1% (Moons) and 91.63% (MNIST).
conclusion: The architecture provides a scalable route to native signed optical computing with constant hardware overhead per multiply-accumulate operation, promising for large-scale incoherent photonic systems.

title: Robust Chance Constrained Complex Zero-Sum Games
authors: Raneem Madani (L2S), Abdel Lisser (L2S), Zeno Toffano
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a unified framework for zero-sum games in which both the pure strategies and the payoff matrices contain complex-valued entries. By leveraging a linear isomorphism between complex and real vector spaces, we extend key results from real-valued convex analysis to the complex domain, establishing the validity of the minimax theorem and the preservation of saddle-point structure. Building on this foundation, we formulate a complex zero-sum game model that enables mixed strategies to interact with the real and imaginary components of the payoff matrix, and we characterize its saddle-point equilibrium through associated primal and dual problems. To incorporate uncertainty, we introduce a complex chance-constrained zero-sum game model (3CP) that handles individual probabilistic constraints defined by complex linear functionals. We first study the 3CP formulation under known exact distributions, focusing on Complex Elliptically Symmetric random variables, which generalize the complex Gaussian family. The framework is then extended to moments-based ambiguity sets, including: (i) distributions with known first two moments, (ii) distributions with unknown second-order moments, and (iii) fully distributed with unknown moments. In all cases, the probabilistic constraints admit deterministic second-order cone representations, ensuring convex feasible strategy sets and enabling explicit characterization of the complex game value. Numerical experiments, including a transmitter--jammer waveform interaction model, show how the proposed framework captures the behavior of complex mixed strategies. Additionally, we evaluate out-of-sample rates and confirm that practical behavior closely aligns with the theoretical guarantees.
tldr: This paper extends zero-sum game theory to complex-valued strategies and payoff matrices, incorporating chance constraints with complex random variables.
motivation: To develop a unified framework for zero-sum games with complex numbers, which arise in signal processing and communications, and to handle uncertainty via chance constraints.
method: Uses linear isomorphism between complex and real spaces to extend convex analysis and minimax theorem; formulates complex chance-constrained zero-sum game models with elliptical distributions and moment-based ambiguity sets, leading to second-order cone representations.
result: Establishes saddle-point equilibria for complex zero-sum games and provides deterministic convex reformulations for probabilistic constraints under various distributional assumptions.
conclusion: The framework enables tractable analysis of complex-valued games with uncertainty, demonstrated on a transmitter-jammer waveform model, with out-of-sample performance matching theory.

title: Vector Invariance And Structural Closure Of Julia-Type Iterations In Clifford Algebra
authors: Orgest Zaka
abstract: ArXiv:2605.20252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a Clifford algebra framework for Julia-type dynamics driven by the geometric product. The nonlinear iteration \[ f() = (\diamond )^p \diamond + , \qquad p \ge 2, \] is studied in a real [MATH]-dimensional inner-product space [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] is a unit vector. The main result reveals a previously unreported invariance phenomenon: although the geometric product generates higher-grade multivector components at intermediate stages, a built-in grade-reduction mechanism ensures complete collapse back to the vector subspace. Consequently, the Clifford Julia operator is shown to be closed on [MATH], and the iteration defines a well-posed nonlinear dynamical system in arbitrary dimensions. This invariance is established through a structural decomposition of the Clifford product and an inductive closure argument, supported by explicit verification in low-dimensional cases and a general proof in [MATH]. The results demonstrate that classical Julia dynamics can be consistently extended beyond the complex plane into higher-dimensional geometric algebra without loss of geometric interpretability. The framework opens a new direction for fractal-type dynamics in Clifford algebras, providing a unified algebraic setting for higher-dimensional invariant-preserving iterative systems.

motivation: To generalize classical complex-plane Julia dynamics to higher-dimensional geometric algebras while preserving geometric interpretability.
method: The authors use a Clifford algebra framework with geometric product iteration, structural decomposition, and inductive closure arguments to prove vector invariance.
